title: One new rule per level
description: The active cumulative word course for the Reading Learner app. Each small level adds one focus; earlier patterns can appear again.
scope: 41 word levels with 240 focus words. Number practice retains its separate ten-level course.
prerequisitesNote: The sequence is cumulative: every level assumes the patterns from all earlier levels. Listed prerequisites highlight additional earlier patterns inside its focus words; they are not a separate route through the course.
startingSkills: The child recognises the ordinary single-letter consonant sounds, including hard c and g, consonant y, and x as ks.
The child can attempt blending simple consonant-vowel-consonant words.
These are starting requirements, not confirmed assessment results. A grown-up checks them before practice.
startingWordsNote: A grown-up can confirm these starter words in settings only when the child already reads them independently. Mastered focus words from the current or earlier levels also qualify as familiar words. Future-level and parked words are outside automatic familiar selection.

roundRecipe.opening: Three familiar words from mastered focus words at or before the current level, or starter words explicitly confirmed by a grown-up.
roundRecipe.focus: Four encounters from the current level's focus bank. Rotate the bank across rounds; the whole level need not fit in one round.
roundRecipe.closing: Three familiar words again. Repeats of known words are allowed.
roundRecipe.reviewSelection: The lists below are examples of earlier words. Automatic selection uses mastered focus words at or before the current level and explicitly confirmed starter words. There is no requirement to use every candidate.
roundRecipe.noKnownWords: Word practice requires at least one mastered focus word at or before the current level, or an explicitly confirmed starter word. If neither is available, a grown-up confirms familiar starters in settings or addresses the starting skills before practice.

completion.description: Only the focus bank determines level completion. Each focus word needs two qualifying first-attempt Yes confirmations for gold mastery. A helped repeat advances the encounter but does not earn a qualifying first-attempt Yes.
completion.familiarWords: Opening and closing words do not add new completion requirements.
completion.earnedProgress: Existing word trophies and earned confirmations are preserved. An already mastered focus word keeps its credit.
completion.restart: The course migration selects the first unfinished focus bank from preserved word progress. A grown-up can choose Level 1 for practice without wiping trophies; level overrides survive reloads.
completion.selfCheck: The record → expected word → Got it? → Yes or record again flow is unchanged. The voice-recognition experiment remains stopped; no reference recordings are required.
completion.ruleChips: Focus encounters show the current level's one primary rule chip. Familiar opening and closing encounters do not introduce a focus chip. Earlier spelling help remains available through each word's sound buttons.

deferredPatterns.reason: Separate spelling cohorts need their own levels; ee and ea should not share a new-rule level.

deferredPatterns.pattern: u-e saying oo and coalescing sounds
deferredPatterns.reason: Keep them separate from the yoo cohort.
baby combines an open syllable, final y and more than one syllable.

deferredPatterns.pattern: Soft c and g, ph and wh
deferredPatterns.reason: Introduce each pattern separately after the core course.

deferredPatterns.pattern: Silent consonants and further consonant teams
deferredPatterns.reason: They are additional correspondences, outside this first map.
music and longer words require more than the core single-syllable patterns.
Words such as the, of, was and have need deliberate separate teaching. Teaching quiet th and buzzy th does not cover the exceptional vowel in the.
live and similar words need context or an explicitly selected meaning before they are suitable focus items.

implementationNotes.before: A word's single numeric level drives both selection and completion.
implementationNotes.after: The active word course has explicit focus banks and familiar-word selection, with one stable progress record per word.
implementationNotes.reason: The same familiar word can support many later levels without gaining new mastery requirements.

implementationNotes.before: Missing canonical words are deleted from stored progress during loading.
implementationNotes.after: All existing word identities remain in the catalog, including parked words. Parked and custom words remain available for grown-up tuning outside this fixed course.
implementationNotes.reason: Deferred words must retain their trophies, attempts and settings.

implementationNotes.before: The old course's numeric level and old one-time migrations describe the ten-level sequence.
implementationNotes.after: The new word-course identity has an explicit migration that preserves word progress and old round history, then selects the first unfinished focus bank. Saved level overrides survive later reloads.
implementationNotes.reason: Old Level 3 cannot silently acquire the meaning of the new Level 3.

implementationNotes.before: Word and number practice share MAX_LEVEL = 10.
implementationNotes.after: Word practice uses 41 levels and a fixed 3 + 4 + 3 round. Number practice keeps ten levels and its configurable round size.
implementationNotes.reason: The two courses have different lesson structures.

implementationNotes.before: Artwork is assigned only to the ten old word levels.
implementationNotes.after: Every active word level has its own assigned picture. The 31 real tank photographs retain their source and licence credits; ten existing pictures mark milestones.
implementationNotes.reason: Every word level has a different, deliberate image assignment.

implementationNotes.before: Sound buttons and family tags cover the existing vocabulary.
implementationNotes.after: Every active focus bank has explicit sound-authoring coverage. Rule introductions, rule-chip replays and this page's previews use the same declared playback steps.
implementationNotes.reason: The word bank and its spoken teaching must express the same sounds.

implementationNotes.before: Rules heard flags and recap selection rely on old rule IDs and numeric levels.
implementationNotes.after: Rule introductions belong to the active course focus. Familiar sections review mastered words from the current or earlier course banks and confirmed starter words. Feedback-only recaps remain exclusive to number rounds.
implementationNotes.reason: Previously heard rules and old numeric levels must not suppress or misdirect the new course.

implementationNotes.before: Several existing rule tags are inconsistent, including both, shall, water and music.
implementationNotes.after: Those four annotations are corrected. The active course has audited sound definitions and demonstrates its rules with recorded sounds and whole-word examples.
implementationNotes.reason: Known annotation errors must not become teaching rules.

sources.title: Department for Education: choosing a phonics teaching programme
sources.purpose: Supports using a systematic progression. This custom map is not a DfE-validated programme.

sources.title: Letters and Sounds
sources.purpose: A phonics reference for correspondences and blending, not an endorsement of this custom word order.

reviewNotes: One new focus means one unfamiliar spelling pattern or blending skill. A word may use several earlier patterns.
Every candidate still needs a child's-eye check for pronunciation and meaning. The word lists do not certify teaching quality.
The focus labels describe these word cohorts, not universal rules for every English word.
A grown-up checks the starting skills and confirms familiar starter words when needed. No extra reference-audio recordings are required.
rulePlaybackNote: Each letter name is spoken slowly on its own, with a short pause. The lesson then demonstrates the recorded phonics sound and whole-word examples. The U-name demonstration uses the real word you. Blending lessons play the separate consonant sounds before the whole word.
artworkNote: Every active word level has its own picture: ten existing space-knight pictures at milestones, with 31 real tank photographs between them. Photo credits are listed below and available from the practice screen.
